title: When the Landfall Sings
premise: Casper Galloway, a mountain guide blacklisted in two countries for a rescue that went wrong, is scraping by as a smuggler's porter when a dying prospector named Ilsa Vey trades him a map to the Meridian's wreck—a salvage ship that sank with a fortune and a passenger manifest that could clear Casper's name—for one promise: deliver the map's truth to her estranged daughter, not sell it. Pursued across six tides by the ruthless salvage fleet captain Odile Marchand, who once trained Casper and knows every trick he knows, Casper must choose between the fortune that could buy back their life and the truth that could finally give them a place in the world. In the end Casper reaches the wreck first but burns the gold ledger, keeping only the manifest, and delivers it to Ilsa's daughter—choosing loyalty to a promise over the price of survival, and finding belonging not in vindication but in being trusted.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent seven seasons in coastal mountain camps listening to guides argue about maps over bad coffee. They write adventure stories about people whose reputations arrive before they do.

chapters.title: The Weight of Invisible Things
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Working a smuggling route through the Sable Passes, Casper is recognized by a border scout and barely escapes, confirming how narrow their world has become. The emotional beat is weary self-containment: Casper has learned to survive by being no one, and we feel both the skill and the loneliness of it.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In a tide-flats waystation, prospector Ilsa Vey, gut-shot and fading, offers Casper a wax-sealed map to the Meridian wreck in exchange for a promise: bring its truth to her daughter Wren in Greyharbor, never sell it. Casper accepts mostly to quiet her. The beat is reluctant obligation taking root.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Reading the map by lamplight, Casper realizes the wreck lies exposed only during six specific low tides—and that the salvage fleet, led by Odile Marchand, has already put out from Port Calloway. First contact with an old crewmate warns Casper that Odile knows the guide is alive. Beat: the clock starts, dread sharpens into purpose.

chapters.title: What Odile Marchand Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Aboard the salvage flagship, Odile reveals she was Casper's mentor and blames them for the disaster that blacklisted them both—though her account differs sharply from what Casper remembers. She burns a village dock for information about the map. Beat: the antagonist gains depth; the past becomes contested territory.

chapters.title: Greyharbor, and the Girl Who Wouldn't Grieve
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Detouring to find Wren Vey, Casper discovers she runs a chandlery and wants nothing to do with the mother who abandoned her. Casper, unable to explain without revealing the map, leaves half a promise kept and half a lie told. Beat: guilt compounds; loyalty and truth begin pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Third Tide Turns Against Us
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Racing along the cliff routes only a guide could read, Casper loses supplies in a storm surge and is forced to accept help from Tam, a young runaway stowaway who idolizes the legendary guide Casper used to be. Beat: warmth arrives uninvited, and Casper realizes invisibility now costs more than exposure.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile interrogates a captured informant and learns the Meridian carried not just gold but a sealed manifest naming officials who framed Casper—and that her own backers want it destroyed. Her loyalty to her fleet wavers against her hunger for leverage. Beat: antagonist and protagonist converge on the same truth from opposite motives.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Drowned Hold
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Diving the half-exposed wreck at slack water, Casper finds the strongbox—but Odile's boats close in, and Tam is taken hostage on the shingle beach. Casper surrenders the map to save the boy, watching six years of survival burn down to one choice. Beat: sacrifice; the climax's hinge.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: POV alternating Casper/Odile. At the final low tide, Odile opens the strongbox expecting gold and finds Casper has already taken only the manifest, leaving a note: the truth was the treasure. Confronted on the drowned deck, Odile must decide whether to kill the last person who knew who she was before the fleet did. Beat: climax—truth versus power, face to face.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Odile lets Casper go, trading silence for the manifest's page bearing her own name. In Greyharbor, Casper gives Wren the whole truth, including the ugly parts, and Wren chooses to believe her mother meant something by it. Casper takes a guiding job under their own name at last. Beat: resolution—belonging earned through honesty, not erasure.
